newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No EU gene maize decision before December-Fischler.
newsitem.headline: No EU gene maize decision before December-Fischler.

text.p: The European Commission will not take a decision before December on whether to approve the sale and release of Ciba Geigy's genetically modified maize, European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Monday.
"New scientific questions have come up which are very important for our fact assessment on this GMO maize and whether it should be allowed or not," Fischler told a news conference.
The Commission has asked scientific committees on food, animal fodder and pesticides to assess the safety of the Swiss chemical company's genetically modified organism (GMO).
"As things stand at the moment, it's likely that it will be by December that we will get the experts' views," he added.

Neither Fischler nor Commission officials questioned after the news conference would give details about what new scientific data had been presented on the maize, which has been approved for release by U.S. authorities.
Fischler said any traders carrying GMO corn in shipments to Europe from this year's U.S. harvest would do so at their own commercial peril until the EU granted its approval.

"It's the Commission's absolute right to examine these issues before the authorisation is given. If companies just let their maize onto ships and send their ships to Europe then that is their commercial risk," he said.

"You cannot simply put before the European Union a 'fait accompli'. All the necessary legal procedures must be completed first and this is wghat we are doing," he added. --Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
